Scenarios.Scenario: Desktop or remote workbench startup discovers built-in and current-profile extensions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Extension service startup awaits system and user scans in parallel before resolving the extension descriptions used to start extension hosts. Each scan stats its source, reads one cache file, and on a miss scans manifests and writes one cache file.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat extension source and read the system extension manifest cache; on a miss resolve the extension directory, read/parse each package manifest and localization resource, then serialize/write one cache file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Warm: one stat and one cache read for the system extension group. Cold: one directory resolution plus manifest/localization reads scaling with the number of built-in extensions, followed by one cache write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same stat, cache read, cold scan, and cache write occurred; the cache file lived under the default profile location instead of that profile's cacheHome.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The scan is on extension-service startup's critical path; system and user groups run concurrently, while manifests within a cold group are scanned with Promise.all.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat the active profile extension manifest, read the user extension cache, and on a miss read the profile manifest and installed extension package manifests before writing one cache file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Warm: one profile/source stat and one cache read for the active profile. Cold: work scales with the effective extensions referenced by that profile, plus application-scoped extensions from the default profile, and ends with one cache write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical operations and cardinality used a cache file under profile.location. The PR changes only the destination path to profile.cacheHome.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in parallel with the system scan but must finish before startup extension discovery resolves.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective number of built-in extensions plus extensions referenced by the active profile after profile-level grouping; system and user groups execute in parallel, and cold per-extension scans are already concurrent.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Two top-level scans run via Promise.all. Cold extension manifest scans within each group also use Promise.all; this concurrency is pre-existing and unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm launches read one cache per system/user group from the new per-profile cache directory. Cache inputs include product version/date/commit, source mtimes, language, and translations, so an application update already invalidates the old-build cache; relocation does not add an extra reusable-cache loss on that update. FileService.writeFile creates missing parent directories recursively, so the new nested location persists successfully.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the startup callers, cache hit/miss branches, parent-directory creation, and per-extension filesystem work were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact extension counts and filesystem latency vary, but no changed mechanism increases cold-scan frequency or manifest-read cardinality after the new cache is populated.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The diff relocates the same two cache files without defeating persistence, increasing scan frequency, or adding startup boundary calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Extension install, uninstall, or metadata update invalidates the affected profile's user manifest cache
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Install/uninstall event listeners invoke invalidation without awaiting the returned promise, so cache deletion is off the operation's awaited critical path; direct invalidate callers also perform one deletion for the matched profile.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Delete extensions.user.cache for the profile whose extensionsResource matches the event's profile location.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One delete attempt per install result or uninstall/metadata invalidation event; profile lookup is in-memory and only the matching profile is deleted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same event loop and one deletion attempt per result/event targeted profile.location; the PR retargets it to profile.cacheHome and suppresses only FILE_NOT_FOUND errors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Event-driven invalidations are fire-and-forget and do not delay install/uninstall completion. A direct awaited invalidate waits for one file deletion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of install results/events, with one cache-file deletion attempt per result; profile count affects only an in-memory match loop.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Batch install listener invocations remain independently fire-and-forget as before; the diff adds no limiter or new fan-out and does not change aggregate deletion cardinality.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful invalidation forces the next scan for that profile to be cold, exactly as before. Missing cache files are now treated as an expected negative result rather than logged/rejected.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: listener registration, loops, matching, and deletion call were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large bulk installs can already issue repeated deletion attempts, but that multiplicity is unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Boundary count, scheduling, and cache invalidation semantics are unchanged; only the cache path and expected-error handling differ.

Scenarios.Scenario: Named or transient profile removal cleans profile data and the newly separated cache directory
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Manual profile deletion awaits will-remove joiners, then the new recursive cache deletion, then the existing recursive profile-data deletion. Transient cleanup removes unassociated profiles concurrently via Promise.allSettled.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recursively delete the removed profile's cacheHome.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One directory deletion per removed profile. In this diff the directory owns at most the built-in and user manifest cache files for that profile.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No separate cache directory existed, so profile removal performed only the existing recursive deletion of profile.location/profilesHome.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly awaited on manual profile-removal latency; transient cleanup runs one such deletion per unassociated transient profile concurrently.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recursively delete profile.location, or profilesHome when only the default remains.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing recursive deletion per removed profile.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same recursive profile-data deletion and ordering after profile association updates.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of profiles removed together; each new cache directory is bounded to the small manifest-cache set currently introduced by this change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Within one removal, cache and profile directory deletion are serialized. Multiple transient profiles are removed concurrently by the pre-existing Promise.allSettled cleanup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Deletion prevents cache retention after profile removal. Missing cache directories are negative-cache misses handled without retries; there is no long-lived retained map or orphaned handle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: removal ordering and all cache writers were searched; only the two manifest cache filenames currently target profile.cacheHome.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem deletion latency varies, but realistic cache directory content from this PR is only one or two files, making the added user-triggered boundary bounded and not a reportable regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The additional awaited deletion is deliberate lifecycle cleanup, one call per removed profile, and bounded to a tiny cache directory.

Scenarios.Scenario: Profile objects are transferred among main, shared, renderer, remote, storage, and import/export preview services
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Startup window/shared-process configuration and profile service initialization serialize and revive profile DTOs; profile events repeat this for changed profile collections. Import/export preview constructs an in-memory profile object.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize/transfer profile DTOs that now contain one additional URI field, cacheHome, and revive that URI in receiving processes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional URI-sized field per profile in startup configuration and profile-change payloads; profile cardinality is the effective collection size.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same profile arrays and events crossed IPC without cacheHome.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Startup recipients must deserialize profile configuration, but the added fixed-size field contributes only constant work per normally small profile.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy cacheHome into export-state profile metadata or construct it for the import preview profile.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One URI reference for the selected export/import-preview profile.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Profile metadata omitted cacheHome; cache bytes were not serialized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Constant-size metadata work; no cache contents are read, copied, or exported.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of configured profiles in startup/event payloads; import/export uses one selected profile.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: IPC payload handling follows existing channel sequencing. The diff introduces no additional call, request, subprocess, network operation, or concurrent burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Only cache location metadata crosses IPC; cache contents are neither eagerly read nor retained in payloads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: DTO revival, channel mapping, startup consumers, and import/export construction were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact profile counts vary, but the per-profile addition is one bounded URI object and no expensive cache data.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The fixed-size serialization increase is negligible and does not alter IPC call cardinality or load cache contents.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review across all 20 changed files and relevant transitive paths. The manifest-cache move preserves warm/cold scan cardinality and persistence; profile removal adds only bounded lifecycle cleanup, and profile DTOs gain one fixed-size URI. No actionable diff-introduced performance regression or blameable regression fix met the reporting threshold.
